business_problem: Managing diverse data and scaling quickly without degrading performance Historically, WFM customers were corporate entities such as large banks and blue-chip companies.
solution_summary: Managing diverse data and scaling quickly without degrading performance Historically, WFM customers were corporate entities such as large banks and blue-chip companies. MongoDB Atlas enables scalability, agility, and improved time to market Playvox wanted to leave behind the slow and cumbersome processes of traditional databases. MongoDB Atlas was a natural fit for the team and its Amazon Web Services environment. Using MongoDB Atlas, Playvox discovered that as a managed, modern database platform, it offers a flexible schema design, and has scaling benefits well suited for high-volume and high-traffic applications. With 100’s of millions records a month to manage, and growing client demands, Playvox knew the deployment of MongoDB Atlas was crucial. Playvox found that it was easy to work with MongoDB Atlas; with operational overheads taken care of, its team is free to innovate and further enhance the company’s products.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores the operational, document, and context data behind Playvox's customer-service and assistant workflows.

data_flow: Application, customer, and workflow data is consolidated in MongoDB Atlas, indexed or enriched where needed, and then delivered to downstream applications, analytics, or AI features through low-latency queries and APIs. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, CRM systems, APIs.
business_outcome: MongoDB Atlas enables developer growth and business evolution Having the freedom to organize high volumes of data is critical, and MongoDB Atlas’s flexibility gave Playvox the opportunity and reason to migrate from relational databases.
architecture_clues: AI agents or assistants are layered on top of the MongoDB data platform.
The deployment integrates with CRM systems.
evidence_quotes: “When you’ve got a traditional audience table with tens or even hundreds of millions of records in it, making schema changes is a traumatic event,”
“It got to the point where we were too scared to make changes, because of the complexity of traditional relational tables.”
“We don’t want to spend time on the plumbing if we don’t have to,”
“That was the most important thing for us.”
